The evidence base is much stronger on continued capture / favoritism than on any genuine anti-corruption turnaround.","evidence":[{"title":"Bangladesh receives $900 million World Bank financing to increase economic and urban resilience for sustainable growth","publisher":"World Bank","date":"June 21, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth","summary":"The World Bank described reforms that would improve procurement, banking oversight, and tax design. This is the clearest positive sign that the government was trying to reduce some corruption channels and improve institutional discipline, but it is still reform intent rather than proof of durable anti-corruption success.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.4"]},{"title":"Bangladesh Investment Development Authority webinar describes changes to encourage economic development and investor trust","publisher":"Bangladesh Investment Development Authority","date":"October 30, 2024","url":"https://www.boi.gov.bd/details/bangladesh-investment-webinar-describes-changes-encourage-economic-development-and-investor-trust","summary":"Officials promoted process changes like a “project ambassador” and smoother investor engagement. This is a limited positive signal for reducing arbitrary favoritism in investment administration, but it is weak evidence because it is official self-description, not independent confirmation of changed behavior.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.4"]},{"title":"Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House said corruption, bribery, bureaucratic hurdles, regulatory obstacles, and state interference constrained private activity. It also described weakened anticorruption enforcement and coercive use of state resources. This is strong evidence against resisting favoritism and elite capture.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.4","4B.4"]},{"title":"Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024","summary":"The report says the ruling party manipulated the online environment and that critics said the legal and administrative environment was politicized. While this is mainly an information-freedom source, it also supports a broader pattern of institutional favoritism and partisan control.","question_ids":["5B.5","4B.6","4B.9"]},{"title":"Bangladesh Development Update - Special Focus: Creating Jobs for a Better Future","publisher":"World Bank","date":"October 1, 2024","url":"https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099104310142425439","summary":"The report says SMEs faced high regulatory costs, weak competition policy, unreliable infrastructure, and limited finance, and it calls for competitive neutrality for state-owned enterprises and streamlined trade policy. This is strong evidence that Bangladesh had not created a clean, fair market order and that anti-monopoly / anti-capture rules were still deficient.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.4"]},{"title":"Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth","publisher":"World Bank","date":"April 2, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r","summary":"The World Bank said investment was being hurt by tight liquidity, import restrictions, higher input costs, and financial-sector vulnerabilities. This supports the view that the business environment was still distorted and that the state had not effectively cleaned up the rules environment for private enterprise.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.4","5B.3"]},{"title":"AL govt created lawless economy","publisher":"The Daily Star","date":"October 31, 2024","url":"https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796","summary":"The white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of bureaucrats, political leaders, and business interests that captured public organizations. This is direct negative evidence for oligarchic capture and politically connected privilege.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.4"]},{"title":"Rooppur Power Plant was AL govt's white elephant: energy sector experts","publisher":"TBS News","date":"October 5, 2024","url":"https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801","summary":"Energy-sector experts described Rooppur as mismanaged and corruption-linked, which supports the view that major state-backed investment decisions were vulnerable to patronage and weak discipline rather than clean competition.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.2","5B.4"]},{"title":"Bangladesh’s defense budget rose 11%...","publisher":"Janes","date":"June 6, 2024","url":"https://www.janes.com/defence-intelligence-insights/defence-news/industry/bangladesh-increases-202425-defence-budget","summary":"Janes notes development spending fell and overall modernization stalled under economic constraints. This is only indirect, but it weakens any claim that state spending discipline was being used to curb patronage or channel resources into broad productive use.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.4"]},{"title":"Reforms and investment messages around Rooppur / nuclear administration","publisher":"The Daily Star / Dhaka Tribune / NEI / Daily Country Today","date":"April-July 2024","url":"https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/consider-setting-2nd-nuclear-power-plant-3580751","summary":"Hasina’s nuclear and regulator-side actions show some technical administration and licensing discipline, but these are sector-specific and do not amount to evidence that the wider political economy was protected from favoritism or connected-business privilege.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.2"]}]}
